transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, good to meet you too. So, man, it’s... it’s a lot, honestly. I’ve been trying to figure out how to explain it because usually I’m really on top of things, you know? I’m an electrician, and in my line of work, you’ve gotta be sharp. But lately... well, what finally pushed me to make this appointment, what finally got me into this chair today, is that I just cannot, for the life of me, keep my focus on a single estimate or a code form anymore. 

And those forms are crucial, right? You mess up a code compliance form and you’re looking at failed inspections, which costs money, delays the whole project, and makes you look bad to the general contractors. But I’ll be sitting there at my desk in the shop, trying to run the numbers, and then—bam—I hear a tool noise out in the bay. Like, the air compressor kicks on, or someone drops a pair of wire strippers, and my brain just completely snaps to that. Or my phone buzzes with a text, and I have to look, and then suddenly I’m not even thinking about the text anymore because I’m thinking about this massive new idea I have for reorganizing the entire workshop. Like, building these custom shelving units for the conduit and the breakers, which is a brilliant idea, don't get me wrong, I've got the whole schematic mapped out in my head...

But the problem is, I get completely pulled off track from the paperwork I was supposed to be doing. Hours go by, I’ve started three other things, and then the jobs start getting all mixed up. I’m putting the materials for a residential job onto the invoice for a downtown office reno, and it’s just... it’s a disaster. I’ve never been this scattered before, and it’s really starting to mess with my livelihood and my reputation, so I figured I had to come in and talk to somebody about it because I can't keep operating like this, it's just not sustainable.
During these times when your focus is all over the place, do you also feel unusually energized or 'up' compared with your normal self?

Oh, yeah. Yeah, absolutely, that's exactly it. It’s like... it’s like someone hooked me up to a 240-volt line, honestly. My whole body is just humming with it. I get into this really big, just completely pumped-up mood where I feel like I can take on the world. I'll be at the shop, and I'll start talking a mile a minute to anyone who will listen about these massive plans I'm putting together. 

Like, recently, I've been pitching everyone on this idea that our little shop is about to become the main solar outfit in town. The whole town! Because I'm looking at the market, right? The tax incentives are there, the residential demand
When you’re feeling this revved up, do you need less sleep than usual?

Oh man, the sleep thing. That's actually one of the craziest parts of all this, because usually, I'm a solid eight-hours-a-night guy. You know, pulling wire and crawling through attics all day, it takes it out of you. You usually hit the mattress and you're out cold. But lately? For months now, honestly, I've been getting by on... I don't know, maybe three or four hours a night? Max. 

And the wild part is, I don't feel tired at all. Not even a little bit. I'll hit the pillow at maybe 1 or 2 AM because I'm just buzzing with all these ideas for the shop and the solar expansion, and then—bam—my eyes just snap open before dawn. It's like 4:30 in the morning and I am just wide awake, completely refreshed, like I just slept a full, deep ten hours. 

I'll literally pop out of bed, make a pot of coffee that I don't even really need because I'm already wired, and I'm just instantly ready to go. I'll sit down at the kitchen table in the pitch black and start pricing out materials for the week—checking the current rates on copper, looking at PVC bulk pricing—and then I'm firing off emails to our suppliers and the general contractors before they're even awake. Or I'll be sketching out another whole system for that solar pitch I was telling you about, just drawing up the schematics, figuring out the inverter loads, right there at the breakfast table. It's like there just aren't enough hours in the day, so my brain just decided to stop needing sleep so I can get all this stuff done, you know? It feels incredibly productive, but then I look at the clock and it's 5 AM and I've already done half a day's work.
When you’re feeling this revved up, have you had experiences where you believed things that other people said weren’t true or realistic?

Well, it’s funny you use the word 'realistic' because, yeah, I’ve been getting into some arguments with the guys at the shop about exactly that. Like, my boss, he thinks I'm getting way ahead of myself, and he's been pretty vocal about it. 

See, lately I just have this... this overwhelming feeling that I am completely ready to take on these massive commercial jobs. And I'm not just talking about, you know, wiring up a little mom-and-pop storefront or changing out some fluorescent ballasts. I'm talking about bidding on these huge, multi-story office build-outs downtown. The real heavy-duty stuff. I keep telling everyone at the shop that we need to pivot right now, that I can handle the estimating, the project management, the whole nine yards. I even started putting together this whole training manual at my kitchen table at like 3 AM, because I feel like I could hire and train a whole new crew of apprentices right now. I just want to bring in like ten green guys and get them all up to speed in a week. I've got the whole curriculum laid out in my head—how I'd teach them complex conduit bending, three-phase systems, commercial load calculations, everything. 

And the guys at work, they're looking at me like I've lost my mind. They keep telling me it's impossible and that I'm not being realistic. And... I mean, I guess, if I really take a step back and force myself to look at it objectively, part of me knows they have a point. Like, I know my licensing and my actual years of experience aren’t quite where they need to be for all that yet. You need a master electrician's license to pull the permits for commercial jobs of that scale, and I'm still a journeyman. I still need a couple more years of logged hours before I can even sit for the master's exam. 

So logically, somewhere in the back of my head, I know I don't have the credentials on paper to be running a ten-man crew on a high-rise. But when I'm in that zone? When my brain is just firing on all cylinders? I just look at the blueprints and I know, I absolutely know, that I can do it better than any master electrician in this city. I just feel like I'm completely ready for it, even if everyone else is telling me to pump the brakes.
Have there been clear periods when you felt like this, separated by times when you were back to your usual self?

Well, see, that's the thing. It hasn't really been like an on-and-off switch lately. Usually, yeah, I'd have a week where I'm really fired up, maybe knock out a bunch of side jobs, and then I'd sort of settle back into my normal rhythm. You know, just regular old me, going to work, coming home, watching a little TV, getting a solid eight hours. 

But this time? This time it's been different. It's been this constant, steady build. Like... like a pressure cooker that's just been slowly heating up and heating up. I'd say it's been going on for about seven months now. Just this relentless energy and all these massive ideas that just won't quit. 

And I can actually pinpoint exactly when it started, too. It was right around the time my business partner and I took out the mortgage for the new workshop and all the heavy equipment. We finally pulled the trigger on getting our own space, you know? We bought this great little commercial property out on Route 9, and we financed a couple of new work trucks, a scissor lift, some really high-end diagnostic gear... the whole setup. 

And man, the day we signed those papers, it was like someone flipped a switch in my brain. I just started thinking, 'Okay, we have the overhead now. We have the mortgage, we have the equipment loans, we need to hustle.' And that hustle just... it just never stopped. It just kept escalating. I started working longer hours, then the sleep started dropping off, then the ideas started getting bigger and bigger. So yeah, for the last seven months, since we took on all that debt for the shop, I haven't really had a break. I haven't gone back to my 'usual self' at all. It's just been this one, long, continuous upward climb, and I don't feel like I'm coming down anytime soon. I just feel like I'm gaining momentum, honestly.
